beats.beat: The company's product range spans four groups: functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals and hard minerals; it calls its diversified product portfolio a competitive strength.

Sales run through a long-term arrangement with corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited, which markets and sells the company's products through its network — the filing describes deriving substantial synergies from this promoter.
How contracts are won: there are no long-term or definitive customer agreements; volume, pricing and other terms are governed by purchase orders, and the same is true for raw-material suppliers.
Customer concentration is high: the top 10 customers accounted for about 59% of revenue from operations in FY15, 57% in FY16 and 59% in FY17.
Exports over the past five years totalled ₹1,068.18 lakh (₹10.68 crore), going to Nigeria, Saudi Arabia and Sri Lanka.

The operating footprint disclosed in the filing includes manufacturing facilities at Plot 347, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara and at Plot 104/3, Thenkasi Road, Pathur Village, Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu, plus administrative offices in Bhuj and Udaipur; the new facility is planned at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia.
Other strengths the DRHP claims: diversified user industries, import substitution, product innovation and continuous R&D, and a strong management team.

beats.beat: The DRHP's restated financial statements are presented in ₹ lakh; this report converts them to ₹ crore for readability, using ₹100 lakh = ₹1 crore.
Profit after tax was ₹1.33 crore in the six months to September 2017, ₹1.75 crore in FY17, ₹0.90 crore in FY16 and ₹1.50 crore in FY15, against losses of ₹0.12 crore in FY14 and ₹0.27 crore in FY13.
Operating cash flow was negative in FY17 at -₹3.50 crore, after +₹8.03 crore in FY16 and +₹4.22 crore in FY15; the six months to September 2017 showed +₹1.25 crore.
Total assets were ₹34.25 crore at September 30, 2017, compared with ₹32.74 crore at FY17 end and ₹30.19 crore at FY13 end.
Basic earnings per share were ₹1.48 for the six months to September 2017, ₹2.43 for FY17, ₹1.46 for FY16 and ₹2.47 for FY15, and negative in FY13 and FY14.
Revenue from operations, EBITDA and a detailed debt schedule were not present in the extracts reviewed; those will be flagged as not disclosed rather than estimated.

beats.beat: The promoters are corporate promoter 20 Microns Limited and individuals Mr. Chandresh S. Parikh, Mr. Atil C. Parikh and Mr. Rajesh C. Parikh.
Promoters hold 89,48,270 equity shares, or 99.76% of the pre-issue paid-up equity share capital; the promoter group excluding promoters holds 21,510 shares, or 0.24%.
At September 30, 2017, issued, subscribed and paid-up capital was 89,70,000 equity shares of ₹10 each (₹897 lakh), against authorised capital of ₹2,000 lakh.
The company has entered into related-party transactions during each of the last five financial years and the six months ended September 30, 2017, as disclosed under Accounting Standard 18.

The filing admits past instances of non-filings, incorrect filings or delays in filing statutory forms with the RoC, and says the company has not yet obtained certain statutory and regulatory approvals for its manufacturing facility at Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara.

Unsecured loans taken by the company, promoters, group companies or associates can be recalled by lenders at any time, and loan agreements carry restrictive covenants and unconditional rights in favour of lenders.
The company, promoters, group company and directors are parties to certain legal proceedings, and contingent liabilities aggregated to ₹29.11 lakh at September 30, 2017.

beats.beat: The company operates in specialty chemicals, which the DRHP says made up about 17% of the Indian chemicals industry at roughly ₹1,000 billion; CRISIL Research estimated the whole Indian chemicals industry at ₹5,800–6,200 billion in fiscal 2017.

The specialty chemicals segment grew at 10–12% CAGR from fiscal 2014 to 2017 and is forecast to grow at 12–14% CAGR going forward; within it, construction chemicals, water chemicals and personal care ingredients are each expected to grow at 15% CAGR, surfactants at 13%, and polymer additives at 10%.
CRISIL Research expects polymer demand to grow at 9–10% CAGR between fiscals 2017 and 2020 and demand for plastic products at 11–13%.
Competition is highly fragmented — SMEs hold 70–75% market share — but only a few Indian players have the scale to compete with global giants on product development and innovation.

The DRHP's macro story leans on rising private consumption (58% of GDP), urbanisation, 7.1% GDP growth in fiscal 2017, 100% FDI in chemicals, and a Draft National Chemical Policy aimed at raising the chemicals sector's share of GDP.
It also acknowledges headwinds: chemicals imports have grown slightly faster than exports (6.4% CAGR vs 6% CAGR), and exports to Europe face strict REACH regulation.
Import substitution is one of the company's stated strengths — relevant because China, a major commodity-chemicals player, has seen stricter environmental regulations since 2015 curb its output.

beats.beat: 20 Microns Nano Minerals is an Indian processor and seller of specialty chemicals — functional additives, chemically modified minerals, soft minerals and hard minerals — with a long-term arrangement under which its corporate promoter, 20 Microns Limited, markets and sells the products through the promoter's network.

The public issue is aimed at listing on NSE's SME platform and is intended partly to fund a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara, and partly to create a public trading market for the shares.
The DRHP names Vivro Financial Services Pvt Ltd as lead manager and Link Intime India Pvt Ltd as registrar.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader in one or two paragraphs: who the company is, what it is selling, and what this IPO is for.

beats.beat: The lead manager named in the DRHP is Vivro Financial Services Private Limited; the registrar is Link Intime India Private Limited.

The stated objects of the issue are: to fund capital expenditure for a new manufacturing facility at Plot 336, GIDC Waghodia, Vadodara; general corporate purposes; and to create a public trading market for the equity shares by listing them on the SME Platform of NSE, called NSE EMERGE, to enhance visibility and brand.
The listing is on the SME platform of NSE, not the main board, per the stated object of the issue.

The extracted DRHP does not disclose the issue size, the split between fresh issue and offer for sale, any selling shareholder, or the price band; this report will describe those as not disclosed rather than estimate them.

beats.beat: Revenue is tied to the corporate promoter's sales network: the company relies on a long-term arrangement under which 20 Microns Limited markets and sells its products, so any disruption to that affiliate relationship would hit the top line directly.

Customer concentration is high — top 10 customers produced roughly 59% of operating revenue in FY15 and FY17 and 57% in FY16 — and no customer is bound by a long-term agreement, leaving volume and price to purchase orders.
Operating cash flow went negative in FY17 (-₹3.50 crore) even though the company was profitable; the DRHP itself flags negative cash flows in previous financial years as a risk factor.
The company does not yet hold all statutory and regulatory approvals for its Plot 9–10, GIDC Waghodia facility and has a history of delayed or incorrect RoC filings, creating exposure to penalties.
Related-party transactions are recurring, and unsecured loans are recallable by lenders at any time; combined with restrictive loan covenants, these could constrain the company's ability to expand.
